### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via getBookTree (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getBookTree, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/book/:name/tree), meta.getBookTree (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta/book/:name/tree, selected by route anchor /meta/book/:name/tree))_
- `content/docs/frontend/data-objectstack.mdx`  _(via /meta/app/:appId/bundle (route, a path literal in MetadataEndpointsConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx`  _(via /meta/book/:name/tree (route, a path literal in MetadataEndpointsConfigSchema))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via /meta/book/:name/tree (route, a path literal in MetadataEndpointsConfigSchema))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via /meta/book/:name/tree (route, a path literal in MetadataEndpointsConfigSchema))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cae71fedfc8f04d35694da55ab74f9d680da0c5f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a993aa0bfde915ee99a6a4ae515b500cb9adf778` — the merge of head `94cfe5128dc57e6e5eb9dc4fd57981f6eddbfd82` into base `cae71fedfc8f04d35694da55ab74f9d680da0c5f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a993aa0bfde915ee99a6a4ae515b500cb9adf778 && git checkout a993aa0bfde915ee99a6a4ae515b500cb9adf778
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cae71fedfc8f04d35694da55ab74f9d680da0c5f 94cfe5128dc57e6e5eb9dc4fd57981f6eddbfd82 && git checkout -B drift-repro cae71fedfc8f04d35694da55ab74f9d680da0c5f && git merge --no-ff 94cfe5128dc57e6e5eb9dc4fd57981f6eddbfd82

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cae71fedfc8f04d35694da55ab74f9d680da0c5f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cae71fedfc8f04d35694da55ab74f9d680da0c5f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `94cfe5128dc57e6e5eb9dc4fd57981f6eddbfd82`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts + packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-app-bundle-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-write-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-config-mount-table.pin.test.ts, docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/api-backend.json (all read as the code the describe makes a claim about; the diff hunks in api-backend.json, the changeset and the regenerated mdx are the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT)

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set: nothing moves. `item: z.boolean().default(true)` is untouched; only the `.describe()` string changes. Right.
- Public surface: the description text in the published `@objectstack/spec` JSON schema and the one row of `content/docs/references/api/rest-server.mdx` change; the regenerated row matches the describe verbatim (`Build Docs` and the generated-output gates are green). Right.
- Measured radius of the switch at the head, counted in the code that reads `metadata.endpoints.item`: the `if (metadata.endpoints.item !== false)` block in `meta-item-read-routes.ts` mounts 4 (`GET /:type/:name/references`, `GET /:type/:name/layers`, `GET /book/:name/tree`, `GET /:type/:name`); `registerPerItemRoute` (returns when the switch is `false`) is called 1 time in `meta-app-bundle-routes.ts` (`GET /app/:appId/bundle`), 2 in `meta-item-write-routes.ts` (`PUT`, `DELETE /:type/:name`) and 6 in `meta-item-history-routes.ts` (`GET /history`, `GET /audit`, `POST /publish`, `POST /rollback`, `GET /diff`, `GET /published`). 4 + 1 + 2 + 6 = 13, the exact set the pin row `metadata.endpoints.item` asserts. `GET /object/:name/state/:field` is registered directly, outside the switch, and the describe does not claim it. Right.
- The describe at the head names exactly those 13, in the mounted-path spelling under the default `/meta` prefix (the same convention its three sibling describes use). Right.
- The reason clause ("registers through the same per-item registrar because every member it serves is the item read's own answer") holds in `meta-app-bundle-routes.ts`: each member, the app included, is fetched the way the plain read's uncached arm fetches it and answered by `createMetaItemAnswer`, the one chain `GET /meta/:type/:name` calls; `metaListSource` only names candidates, each then answered through that chain. The `items` switch removes `GET /:type` alone, so the bundle does not ride it. Right.
- Checklist item `api-backend.rest-metadata-config-contract`: steps[7] enumerates the same 13 in `{prefix}` spelling, acceptance[2].clause says thirteen and names the bundle, the variants row says `(13 mounts)`, revision 8 to 9 with a history entry. The title's `prefix moves every metadata mount` agrees with the `api.enableMetadata` pin row (20 routes) and with acceptance[1], which asserts the whole table re-bases; `eleven` was stale. Right.
- Check-runs on the head at this read (re-fetched): 56 success, 12 skipped, 1 in progress (`Test Core (3/8)`), 0 failed. The in-progress shard is stated as pending, not assumed green.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28934-endpoints-item-bundle-describe.md`: `@objectstack/spec` patch, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in both the changeset body and the PR body. A describe string changes no accepted key, value or default, so the kind is `none` and `none` takes patch (AGENTS.md changeset rule 3). `@objectstack/rest` publishes nothing from this diff (its CHANGELOG history rows naming twelve routes are a record, not drift). `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards are success. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation 1 (title `prefix moves eleven mounts` to `every metadata mount`): answered. The seat amended the claim's file surface to the whole item (card comment 6569713808, Amended paragraph), the default table pins twenty metadata mounts, and acceptance[1] asserts the whole table. Accepted.
- Dev deviation 2 (`check:dev-prereqs` NOT MEASURED): answered. A whole-workspace boot precondition; the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts and the relevant gates are green.
- `open_questions`: none.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (three stale "twelve" comments: the `registerPerItemRoute` docblock in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, the header and row comment of `rest-config-mount-table.pin.test.ts`, the `item` note in `packages/spec/liveness/metadata_endpoints.json`): answered as outside `hits` and outside the claim, which excluded the mount code (stop on breach held). Escalated to the seat's follow-up finding, which the seat said it files, with one addition from this read: `packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts` line 114 says `8 registerPerItemRoute( calls`; the head has 9 (1 bundle, 2 writes, 6 history). None of the four is parsed by a gate; all four are should-fix in the follow-up, not in this PR.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts`, judged against the ruling it implements (triage 6569524266: the radius is intended, the declaration moves) and its first consumers, the mount code and the mount-table pin:

- Holds. The `endpoints` block header promises that each describe enumerates every mount its switch takes; at the head the `item` describe and the measured 13-route radius are the same set, in matching names, and the header itself counts nothing, so it is rightly untouched.
- Tried to break it: (a) could the bundle ride `items` or `api.enableMetadata` alone rather than `item`? No: it registers through `registerPerItemRoute`, and the `items` pin row removes `GET /:type` only. (b) Does the describe over-claim? No: the FSM read is not named, and no other route goes through the per-item registrar. (c) Does the reason clause assert something the code does not do? No, the bundle module's own header and handler say and do the same. (d) Does any test pin the old twelve-route sentence? None in `packages/spec`, `packages/qa` or `packages/rest`; the dogfood harness reads the item by acceptance index. (e) Does the checklist consumer disagree with the describe? No, steps[7], acceptance[2] and the variant row carry the same 13.
- should-fix (pre-existing wording, not introduced here, not blocking): the history-family list in the describe carries no methods, so `/publish` and `/rollback` read as if they were `GET`s beside the explicit `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE` of the item read, while the pin spells them `POST`. Fold into the seat's follow-up or leave; it does not change the set.
- No must-fix.
